title: Greatest miser ever was actually afraid to lay out 4d
html_source: A miser, coming from the Latin word miser, meaning “unhappy” (note the presence of the word in “miserly”), in Modern English and other languages has come to refer to someone who is afraid of spending money and prefers to save it, no matter how little the cost is. When Molly calls Leopold the “greatest miser” here, she means that he was even afraid to spend 4d, or 4 pence, which has always been a small amount of money in Britain. There are 100 pence to the British pound. As of the time of writing this in 2024, 4 pence is roughly 5¢, and 4 pence from 1924 is worth about $3.92 (£3.05).
